hypotheses.reasoning: Before 06:10, catalog-svc was healthy: batch requests finished in about 20–85ms and there are no warnings. Starting at 06:10:12, the third-party translation API (api.translate.example) returned 502/503 errors quickly instead of timing out. At 06:11:57 catalog-svc opened its circuit breaker for that API (87% failure rate). With the breaker open, catalog-svc answered requests with 503s. search-api's CatalogClient.getBatch then failed with 'catalog-svc returned 503 (circuit open)', and web-bff returned 503s on GET /search. A half-open probe at 06:24:39 still got a 503, which shows the provider was still down. I found no deploy lines. The analytics-forwarder 429s started earlier (06:05:37) but are on an unrelated ingest path and don't connect to the search failures.
Some web-bff 503s took 5–15s, which could suggest hanging upstream calls. But the translation API failed fast with 5xx, so this reads better as an outage than as a timeout.
The analytics-forwarder 429 retry loop could be a retry storm, but it doesn't touch the search path. This looks like a red herring.

verdict.recommendedAction: Confirm the outage with the translation provider (api.translate.example) and check their status page. Change catalog-svc so that when the translation API is down it returns untranslated or cached product data instead of a 503, so search keeps working. After the provider recovers, check that the circuit breaker closes again.
